subject: Deployment isolation decision inputs & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Amy Johnson <amy.johnson@curahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Jun 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment isolation decision inputs & next steps

Hi Amy — thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum with the security and infra teams at CuraHealth:

- Recap: you want strong data isolation and minimal cross-tenant access for PHI workflows, prefer no shared-control-plane artifacts touching customer data, and your procurement org wants evidence for KMS residency, network egress, and audit logs.
- Options we discussed: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (isolated GPUs & tenant-level separation), Private VPC / on-prem (full network isolation + customer-controlled VPC).

Proposal / next steps:
1) For pilot: run Dedicated capacity with private control plane + VPC peering to reduce operational overhead but preserve isolation.
2) Parallel: schedule a 60-min ops workshop (network, KMS, audit log owners) to validate firewalls, egress rules, and keystore boundaries.
3) We’ll compile a short evidence packet (SOC2 excerpts, network diagrams, KMS residency explanation, and a short one-pager comparing Dedicated vs Private VPC tradeoffs).

Can you confirm: who from your security/infra team should join the ops workshop (names + emails), and is the preferred pilot start target the week of July 14?

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-vs-vpc-one-pager.pdf (summary), I’ll follow up with the evidence packet by Wednesday.

—Marissa

From: Amy Johnson <amy.johnson@curahealth.com>

Date: Sun, 29 Jun 2025 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment isolation decision inputs & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the recap and clear next steps. A few clarifying points from security/infra:

- Our security team requires that all customer keys remain in our KMS (BYOK) for production. For pilot, we are open to a managed KMS but need a clear migration path to BYOK in the Private VPC model.
- We need documentation on what metadata (if any) leaves our environment to Redwood control plane in Dedicated. Even small identifiers can be a blocker for our compliance team.
- Network egress: can you confirm whether any model telemetry or tokenized logs are routed through a Redwood-managed endpoint in a different region? We have strict EU/US routing requirements for certain datasets.
- SLAs: procurement will want a runtime SLA and options for RPO/RTO for the POC (esp. if PHI is in scope).

For the ops workshop: please invite our infra leads — Michael Perez (m.perez@curahealth.com) and Lena Ortiz (l.ortiz@curahealth.com).

Attaching our initial questionnaire so you can see the more detailed asks (CuraHealth-Security-Questions.pdf).

Amy

Head of Product (AI) | CuraHealth

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Jun 2025 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment isolation decision inputs & next steps

Amy — great, thanks for the details and for naming the infra leads. Short answers up front and then a proposed evidence package:

- BYOK: supported for Private VPC and we offer a migration plan from Redwood-managed KMS to customer-managed keys for Dedicated->Private cutover. We’ll include the migration steps and timeline in the packet.
- Metadata & control plane: for Dedicated we isolate tenant identifiers and do not persist raw customer content in the control plane. We will provide a network diagram and a short data flow map showing exactly what bits cross control plane boundaries.
- Telemetry/egress: default telemetry is anonymized aggregate metrics routed to regional endpoints; no raw token streams are shipped. We’ll include the telemetry schema and routing table.
- SLA/POC: we can provide a POC SLA template and include options for elevated uptime during the pilot.

Evidence packet (I’ll assemble these and drop to you by Wed):
- SOC2 excerpt (relevant sections)
- Network topology diagram (Dedicated vs Private VPC)
- KMS migration plan (Dedicated->Private)
- Telemetry schema & regional routing table
- Draft POC SLA + ops workshop agenda

Next practical step: 1) confirm workshop attendees (Michael & Lena confirmed) 2) proposed windows: July 8–10 (ops deep-dive) or July 15–17 (pilot kickoff). Which works best for your team?

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-vs-vpc-one-pager.pdf

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Amy Johnson <amy.johnson@curahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment isolation decision inputs & next steps

Thanks team — adding a quick cost/ops data point to help prioritize Dedicated vs Private VPC for the pilot:

- Ballpark for a 3-month pilot (Dedicated pool sized for ~10 concurrent inference workers, modest KV cache): $22k–28k/month, plus one-time onboarding (network setup & security review) ~ $6–8k.
- Private VPC/on-prem: higher initial setup (network, firewall, HSM/KMS integration) — typically $50k+ one-time plus higher monthly infra ops depending on customer-managed resources.

If the goal is to validate model behavior and integration quickly with lower procurement friction, Dedicated for pilot + migration path to Private VPC is usually the fastest path. If CuraHealth policy requires BYOK from day one and no control-plane metadata, we’ll prioritize Private VPC and can run a compressed onboarding.

Question for Amy: what peak TPS/QPS should we size for in the pilot (est. concurrency + typical prompt size)? That will materially affect the Dedicated sizing and cost.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Amy Johnson <amy.johnson@curahealth.com>

Subject: Re: Deployment isolation decision inputs & next steps

Marissa / Ben — thanks, that aligns with our thinking. Quick answers and next asks:

- Pilot sizing: baseline 5–8 concurrent inference workers, peak 20 concurrent; prompts average ~120 tokens.
- Procurement note: CuraHealth will require BYOK for production; for pilot we can accept Redwood-managed KMS provided we have a documented migration path and contractual language on key handover.
- Preference: we want to converge on Dedicated pilot with a formal migration-to-Private plan documented and a guarantee that certain metadata fields will never be persisted by the control plane. If you can codify the metadata scope we’ll share with compliance.

Next steps agreed:
1) Schedule ops workshop — July 8 at 10am PT (Michael Perez, Lena Ortiz to join).
2) Redwood to deliver evidence packet and the migration plan by Wed (July 2).
3) Procurement to start draft SOW/POC paperwork — I’ve attached our POC request doc (CuraHealth-POC-Request.docx).

I’ll also loop in procurement once we have the evidence packet. Looking forward to the workshop.

Best,
Amy
